name: Oculomotor Apraxia

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical diagnostic criteria for Oculomotor Apraxia

criteria.description: Inability or marked difficulty to initiate voluntary horizontal saccades
Use of compensatory head thrusts to overcome saccadic initiation failure
Preserved reflexive eye movements such as vestibulo-ocular reflex
No evidence of structural brain lesions on neuroimaging explaining the ocular motor deficit

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of impaired voluntary saccadic initiation with compensatory head thrusts in the absence of structural brain lesions
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical and supported by neuro-ophthalmological examination and imaging.

searchTerms: cannot start quick horizontal eye movements

pathognomonic.symptomName: Compensatory head thrusts to initiate gaze shifts
searchTerms: head jerks to help move eyes
normal eye reflex with head movement
difficulty starting up and down eye movements
eye shaking when trying to look sideways

common.symptomName: Delayed initiation of voluntary eye movements
searchTerms: slow start of voluntary eye movements

common.symptomName: Head nodding or bobbing during gaze shifts

occasional.notes: May be present in syndromic forms

searchTerms: eye movement disorder with muscle spasms

laboratory: Possible elevated alpha-fetoprotein in some syndromic forms
imaging: Normal brain MRI or mild cerebellar atrophy in some cases
No structural lesions causing ocular motor deficits
genetic: Mutations in AOA1 (APTX), AOA2 (SETX), or other genes in syndromic forms
other: Neuro-ophthalmological examination demonstrating saccadic initiation failure

distinguishingFeatures: Vertical gaze palsy rather than isolated saccadic initiation failure
Presence of postural instability and parkinsonism
Involuntary rhythmic eye movements without saccadic initiation failure

redFlags: Sudden onset of oculomotor apraxia symptoms
Presence of structural brain lesions on imaging
references: Mori S, et al. Oculomotor apraxia: clinical features and genetic heterogeneity. Neurology. 2012.
Klockgether T. Oculomotor apraxia and related disorders. J Neurol. 2010.
